channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Affiliate links on Instagram Reels and YouTube explained
item.description: An affiliate link pays the creator a commission when you buy through it, and since 16 November US creators can put Amazon affiliate links right into Instagram Reels and feed posts, as YouTube creators already can with tagged products.

item.title: Kindle vs Kobo for Libby library books and EPUB files explained
item.description: The main difference between a Kindle and a Kobo is how you get books onto it: Libby library loans reach a Kindle only in the US, while Kobo has Libby built in for 13 countries and opens EPUB files directly.

item.title: Apple outage on 17 November: iCloud sign-in, App Store and Apple Pay hit
item.description: Many Apple users couldn't sign in to iCloud, download apps or use Apple Music on 17 November, and some were signed out of their iPhone or Mac. Apple said an internal update caused the outage and that many systems were back up later that day.

item.title: AirTag in checked luggage: TSA rules and sharing it with your airline
item.description: An AirTag is allowed in checked and carry-on bags in the US, because its small coin battery stays inside the tracker, and since iOS 18.2 you can send its location to more than 50 airlines when a bag goes missing.

item.title: ChatGPT GPT-6.2: new Astra and Sol models for Plus and Pro users
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT and Codex on 17 November for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users. Astra is meant for hard, long projects, Sol for everyday writing and coding.

item.title: Disney Plus Hulu app merger: one app with live TV in December
item.description: Disney says Hulu's last missing parts, its live TV service and some premium add-ons, move into the Disney+ app in December, giving subscribers what it calls a fully unified experience. It announced this with its quarterly earnings on 17 November.

item.title: Dithering camera app DIITR shoots retro pixel photos and video
item.description: DIITR is a new $1.99 iPhone camera app that applies dithering, the dotted pixel look of old screens and printers, live in the viewfinder for photos and videos. It was #61 in Photo & Video on the US App Store's paid chart on 17 November.

item.title: Dreadcast weather radar app puts storms and wildfires on one map
item.description: Dreadcast is a free weather app that starts with the radar map, with layers for satellite, wind, temperature, tropical storms, wildfires, earthquakes and volcanoes. It was #100 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 17 November.

item.title: Emulators on iPhone explained: Delta, RetroArch and what's allowed
item.description: Since April 2024 Apple has let retro game emulators like Delta and RetroArch into the App Store, but the apps come without games, and playing copies of games you download from the web is usually against copyright law.

item.title: Ethos family routine app shares chores and schedules on iPhone
item.description: Ethos is a new planner for your own weekly routine and the household's: shared routines, rotating chores and a shared shopping list, on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. It's free to use, and Ethos Plus costs 99 cents a month, 4.99 dollars a year or 12.99 dollars once.

item.title: Final Cut Pro 13 update adds MotionVFX effects for Creator Studio
item.description: Final Cut Pro 13 now includes thousands of MotionVFX themes, transitions, titles and effects, which used to cost up to 350 dollars a year on their own. The new features are only in the Creator Studio version, not the one-time purchase.

item.title: Gemini Tasks now free: the AI agent no longer needs AI Pro
item.description: Tasks, the Gemini app's agent that carries out jobs for you, is free from 17 November in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India; before, it needed an AI Pro plan. It used to be called Spark.

item.title: Google Wallet iPhone app is out in the US, without tap to pay
item.description: Google Wallet is now a free iPhone app in the US for tickets, boarding passes, loyalty cards, receipts and package tracking. You can't use it to tap and pay in shops on iOS.

item.title: iPhone Duo face unlock vs Face ID: how the new option differs
item.description: The iPhone Duo's new face unlock in the iOS 27.3 beta uses an ordinary front camera instead of Face ID's depth sensors, so Apple keeps it to the Lock Screen, asks for Touch ID again after about 45 minutes and warns that it's less secure than Touch ID or Face ID.

item.title: Menu translator app BADè reads menus and signs on your photo
item.description: BADè is a new $9.99 iPhone app for travelers that shows the translation of a menu, street sign or pharmacy label right on the photo you take. It was #83 in Travel on the US App Store's paid chart on 17 November, a day after it came out.

item.title: Netflix no longer available on older Sony Blu-ray players and receivers
item.description: Sony switched off network services such as Netflix and Spotify on a list of older Blu-ray players, AV receivers, soundbars, home theatre systems and speakers on 17 November. Downloaded services and their icons may stop working or disappear from 18 November.

item.title: Northern lights app Aurora Chance gives one number for tonight
item.description: Aurora Chance is a new free iPhone app that turns aurora, cloud and darkness data into one 0 to 100% chance of seeing the northern lights tonight where you are, with a verdict of Go out, Maybe or Not tonight. It was #60 in Weather on the US App Store's free chart on 17 November.

item.title: Opera Neon builds browser extensions from a chat, no coding needed
item.description: Opera's AI browser Neon can now make a browser extension from a description you type in its chat. It shows a preview first, and you install the result with one click.

item.title: Optimizely hack put malware on CNN, BBC and Zoom websites
item.description: On 16 November, malicious code reached visitors of 178 organisations' websites, including Zoom, the BBC, CNN, IKEA, HSBC and Equifax, through Optimizely, a tool sites use to test page designs. It tried to swap crypto wallet addresses, copy card details and attack older iPhones and iPads.

item.title: Pixel camera not working after Android 17 November update
item.description: Some Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL owners report a black camera screen or a Camera app that won't open after Google's November update, Android 17 QPR2. Google hasn't confirmed the problem or released a fix.

item.title: Proton Lumo desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux can work with your files
item.description: Proton's AI assistant Lumo now has a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux that can use your local files, connected apps and scheduled tasks. For each connection you decide whether Lumo acts by itself, asks first or is blocked.

item.title: RadPad notebook app turns your notes into a 90s binder
item.description: RadPad is a new $1.99 iPhone and iPad notes app made to look like a 1990s school binder, with a randomly printed cover and loose-leaf pages. It was #51 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 17 November.

item.title: Remoqa: free remote desktop app to help family with their PC
item.description: Remoqa is a new remote desktop app in public beta for Windows, Mac and Linux that lets you reach your own computer or help friends and family, with end-to-end encrypted sessions. The free plan covers up to 3 devices and one session at a time.

item.title: Santander Cycles app: new London bike hire app with QR unlock
item.description: London's Santander Cycles bike hire moved to a new app, TfL Santander Cycles, made by Lyft, on 17 November; the old app is no longer available. You unlock a bike by scanning its QR code and can pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay.

item.title: The Weather House: weather app with a wooden chalet for iPhone and Mac
item.description: The Weather House shows your local weather under an illustrated wooden chalet, with figures that step out as the air gets drier or more humid, for $3.99 on iPhone, iPad and Mac. It was #26 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 17 November.

item.title: Tripod podcast app for iPhone: an inbox and automatic queues
item.description: Tripod, a new iPhone podcast player from indie developer Ben McCarthy, puts new episodes in an inbox where you keep or skip each one. It came out on 11 November and is free to download.

item.title: Uber Eats drone delivery starts near Houston with Zipline
item.description: Uber Eats drone delivery with Zipline started on 17 November in Spring, Texas, a suburb of Houston: you tap a new Drone icon in the app and the order is lowered into your yard on a tether. Dallas is next, and dozens more US cities are planned.

item.title: WhatsApp cloud backup on Android in testing: 2 GB free storage
item.description: WhatsApp is testing its own cloud backup on Android, so chats can be backed up on WhatsApp's servers instead of Google Drive, with 2 GB free. It's in beta version 2.26.46.4 for some testers, spotted by WABetaInfo; WhatsApp hasn't said when everyone gets it.

item.title: 10 new graphic design apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten design and drawing apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Graphics & Design charts this week, from the 3D renderer RAYS to Wallmix's wallpapers and widgets.

item.title: 10 new music apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from chord and synth instruments to metronomes and retro music players for your Apple Music library.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These photo and video apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from RAW editors and film looks to a photo booth and a camera trick that gets kids to look at the lens.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a 3D CAD app to focus timers, planners and a family chore chart.

item.title: 10 new weather apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Ten weather apps that came out in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from Snow Day Radar's snow day odds to SkyWX's radar and alerts.

item.title: 6 new education apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Six learning apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Education charts this week, from the CrowCards flashcards to a plant explorer.

item.title: 7 new navigation and GPS apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven navigation apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Navigation charts this week, from a trail ride tracker to a speed camera warner.

item.title: 7 new travel apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Seven travel apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from Watchmen's camera map to an offline voice translator.

item.title: 8 new entertainment apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: Eight entertainment apps released in the last 60 days rose into the US App Store's Entertainment charts this week, including Jitless for PC games and Roku's new official app.

item.title: 8 new utility apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, most of them made for the foldable iPhone Duo, from Safari extensions to desk clocks and a fold counter.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Health & Fitness charts this week, from lifting logs and a calorie tracker to Apple Watch tools for naps, counting and blood oxygen.

item.title: 9 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Lifestyle charts this week, from a retro fridge wallpaper to a phone lock for nights out.

item.title: Android Fast Switch may let you use one SIM on two phones
item.description: Code in a recent update of Google's SIM Manager app points to Android Fast Switch, which would move your mobile service to whichever of your phones you unlock, according to an APK teardown by Android Authority. Google hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: Any Day Now: a countdown app for iPhone with widgets and Live Activities
item.description: Any Day Now counts down to trips, exams, birthdays and other dates, each with its own colours or a cover photo. It was #54 in Productivity on the US App Store's paid chart on 17 November.

item.title: Apple TV app adds free video podcasts in iOS 27.3 beta 2
item.description: The Apple TV app has a new section for video podcasts in Apple's second iOS 27.3 developer beta, and only free shows appear there. Apple also plans more video podcasts in its Podcasts app.

item.title: Beyond Notes markdown notes app for Mac, iPhone and iPad
item.description: Beyond Notes is a new markdown notes app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that shows headings, lists and tables as a finished page while you type, and saves every note as a plain text file in your own iCloud Drive. Your first 50 notes are free.

item.title: Budget apps that connect to your bank vs offline trackers explained
item.description: A budget app either reads your bank and card transactions through a link, as Gemini now can through Google Wallet, or works only with what you type in, and that choice decides how much it sees, where your numbers are stored and what you give up in return.

item.title: ChatGPT account suspended for 24 hours over child abuse prompts
item.description: ChatGPT now warns people who try prompts that sexualize children, points them to support, and suspends the account for 24 hours; doing it again can get the account removed for good. OpenAI announced it on 16 November with a free image classifier for selected companies.

item.title: ChatGPT travel booking may come: OpenAI hires a travel team
item.description: OpenAI is hiring engineers to build travel into ChatGPT, with a job listing for screens that compare stays and transport using live prices and availability, Skift reports. OpenAI hasn't announced a travel feature.

item.title: Copper landline switch off: what replaces your home phone and alarm
item.description: AT&T and Verizon have started switching off old copper landlines area by area, and their replacements keep your number but run on home power with a backup battery, so alarms, medical alert devices and cordless phones need a check before your date.

item.title: Crate Apple Music library app shows your albums as records
item.description: Crate is a new $14.99 app that turns your Apple Music library into a room of records, picking albums back up at the song and second you stopped. It was #73 in paid Music apps on the US App Store on 16 November.

item.title: Create My Widget on Pixel 10 and 11: how to get it early
item.description: Google's Create My Widget app, which builds a home screen widget from a description you type, can now be installed early through a beta on the Google Play Store. It works on the Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series, not the Pixel 10a.
